messages:
Maria R.: Heads-up — I'm putting together a proposal for a telemetry compaction + retention rewrite to cut console storage costs and speed up dashboards. Need quick takes on denorm vs join and a safe migration path. TL;DR: keep raw envelopes short-term (7d) + compact per-route aggregates for longer windows.

Kevin L.: Quick q — if we aggregate per-route-minute, we lose per-request traces used by some debug UIs. Which queries can we realistically sacrifice?

Maria R.: Good call. Plan is: raw envelopes for 7d for debugging + billing accuracy, 90d of minute/hour aggregates for dashboards and alerting. Rare deep-dive queries will still be possible via export.

Samir P.: What are the concrete schema changes? add route_profile_id and some precomputed metric blob? Also quotas rely on per-token counts — how do we keep billing correctness?

Maria R.: Proposed schema changes: add route_profile_id (bigint), add compact_metrics (jsonb) for per-minute aggregates, and a small payload_small boolean flag. Backfill via dualwrite + streaming compactor then batch backfill for historical ranges. Example DDL: 
```
ALTER TABLE telemetry_events ADD COLUMN route_profile_id bigint;
ALTER TABLE telemetry_events ADD COLUMN compact_metrics jsonb;
```

Julia B.: Dualwrite worries me — extra tail latency and more places to fail. We'll need a robust client lib and retries.

Maria R.: Agreed. Dualwrite will be a controlled library change in ingest service behind a feature flag, synchronous to primary path but async to secondary with bounded retry. We'll canary by route.

Nora T.: Frontend impact: dashboards must opt into aggregated endpoints. Also joining route metadata at query time is expensive; denormalizing route_name or route_label into event rows would avoid runtime joins but costs more storage. Thoughts?

Kevin L.: Denorm route_name into rows but keep it small (interned dictionary / short id) — far cheaper than repeated joins for hot dashboards. We can compress with dictionary encoding.

Samir P.: Backfill plan for aggregates: windowed idempotent jobs. Example aggregation pseudocode: 
```
INSERT INTO compact_agg (route_profile_id, ts_min, metrics)
SELECT route_profile_id, date_trunc('minute', ts) AS ts_min,
 jsonb_build_object('requests', count(*), 'tokens', sum(tokens))
FROM telemetry_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY 1,2
ON CONFLICT (route_profile_id, ts_min) DO UPDATE SET metrics = EXCLUDED.metrics;
```

Maria R.: Rough cost estimate for backfill: scanning ~1B rows (~10TB) if we need 2 years. Run on read replicas, throttle concurrency. Compute ~$2k (short-run) + ~500GB temp storage. Open to alternatives if infra costs too high.

Julia B.: Can we reduce backfill by doing streaming compaction from Kafka for the last N months and only run batch for older cold range? That would cut the heavy scan.

Kevin L.: Yes — combine streaming compactor (continuous) + one-time batch for historical tail. Streaming also gets us near-real-time agg.

Nora T.: Quotas: keep raw per-token traces for billing accuracy 30d. Aggregated tokens acceptable after that for quota dashboards. Need to note in runbook.

Maria R.: Rollout proposal: 1) add columns (no lock long) 2) dualwrite + streaming compactor in canary 3) shadow-read dashboards for a subset of routes 4) run parallel backfill in low-priority job pool 5) flip read path per-route 6) cleanup raw rows after retention window.

Samir P.: I'll prototype compaction job and the idempotent upsert pattern. Will include checkpointing and chunking by ts range.

Julia B.: I'll implement a frontend adapter to switch between raw and agg endpoints and add an override for power-users.

Kevin L.: I'll own the dualwrite library spec + PR. Will add metrics for write success/failure and per-route tail latency fence.

Nora T.: I'll run a query audit of the top 20 console queries to ensure none break after aggregation.

Maria R.: I'll collate this into a migration doc + runbook with safety gates and rollback steps. Proposed timeline: prototype next sprint, canary next month, full flip in ~8 weeks if green. @Kevin L., @Samir P., @Julia B., @Nora T. sound OK? :thumbsup:

eng-platform-bot: Reminder — create #inc-migration channel for escalation and add the playbook template here: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/migration-template
